25.$description: The dark ramp inverts — 0 is the page and higher steps lift off it — so these sit the same proportion along 0 -> 100 as their light counterparts.

50.$description: The dark ramp inverts — 0 is the page and higher steps lift off it — so these sit the same proportion along 0 -> 100 as their light counterparts.

full.$description: Maximum roundness. Completes the numeric scale so every semantic radius alias resolves to a plain number.

None.$description: Flush edges: sidebars, navbars, table shells, anything meeting a viewport edge.

Marker.$description: Small marks that sit inside something else: badges, checkboxes, colour swatches.

Control.$description: Interactive controls: buttons, inputs, selects, list rows, toasts, tooltips. The workhorse role - repoint this one alias to change how round the product feels. Moved from radius.100 (8) to radius.200 (16) on 2026-08-28; web was already 16, so that change converged iOS, Android and Figma onto it.

Container.$description: Cards and dialogs: a surface that holds controls. Deliberately rounder than Control — the two were both 16, so a 44px field and a 400px card drew the same corner and the role distinction was cosmetic.

Panel.$description: Large panels and sheets, mostly the Product / SDK map surfaces.

Pill.$description: Fully rounded: chips, avatars, switches, segmented controls.

Subtle.$description: Container edges: cards, popovers, menus, dialogs, drawers, toasts, list rows, the file dropzone. Soft on purpose, about 1.6:1 against the page in both modes, because a container is told apart by its surface and shadow, not its outline. Until 2026-09-03 Figma painted these with foreground/500 and the web with background/200; this alias is now the only place the colour lives.

Input.$description: Boundaries of things you interact with: inputs, checkboxes, radios, switch, slider and progress tracks, swatches, the toast action. Held to WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 against the page: 4.2:1 light, 5.7:1 dark. background/400 reads 2.997 and fails by three thousandths, which is why this is foreground/500. The web used background/200 here before 2026-09-03 and did not meet 3:1.

surface.$description: The quiet field an emotional label sits on — a tag, a counter, a status pill. Paired with onSurface it clears 4.5:1 in both modes; the emotional ramps invert between the two files, so one alias is right in both.

onSurface.$description: Ink on the matching surface. Never on the page: on white it is the wrong end of the ramp.

text.$description: The emotion as text or a glyph on the page itself — white or either grey a panel, card or sheet paints (background/0, /50, /100). The step differs per emotion because the ramps reach 4.5:1 on background/100 at different places: success and alert 900, informative 800, danger 700, themed 600. Measured on white alone they were one step lighter, and four of six failed on a sheet's grey. The product draws success at 600, which is 2.74:1 even on white.

Raised.$description: A surface lifted just off the page: cards, list rows, a file row. Barely there on purpose — the surface and its border do the work, and the shadow only says it is not painted on.

Floating.$description: A control floating over content it does not belong to: map chrome, a search bar over a map, a status message. This is the role the MapScale prototype had to invent for itself, at four depths of a blue-tinted ramp, because nothing here existed.

Overlay.$description: Above everything, with the page dimmed or ignored behind it: menus, tooltips, popovers, dialogs. The heaviest step the scale has.

System.$value: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, "Noto Sans", sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji"
System.$description: The default. Resolves to SF Pro on Apple platforms, Roboto on Android and Segoe UI on Windows. ui-sans-serif leads and system-ui follows it rather than standing alone, because bare system-ui has resolved to fonts with broken non-Latin coverage on some Linux and ChromeOS builds.

Brand.$description: Readex Pro, opt-in. Nothing loads it today: there is no @font-face, no webfont link and no font file in the repo, so web has been falling through to generic sans-serif. Using it means shipping the file and measuring its metrics - see scripts/measure-font-metrics.mjs.

Mono.$value: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace
Mono.$description: Code, coordinates, IDs and anything that wants to align in columns.

quick.$description: A state's small change: a border, a colour, a control appearing.

standard.$description: A layout change: a sheet between detents, a row changing form.

deliberate.$description: A large move across the screen: a panel entering, the AI search docking.

standard.$description: Ease out then settle: what moves between detents and forms.

emphasised.$description: A small overshoot: a chip or a mode popping into place.

Category.$description: The taxonomy's eight quick-access colours (measured from the published 10.12.0 sprite atlas's section markers, light and dark alike), for a category's tile, chip and pin. Accent draws icons and strokes; Fill fills a count pill or counter; OnFill is the ink on that fill, chosen so the digits reach 4.5:1 (scripts/check-token-contrast.mjs holds it).

Yellow.$description: A filled pill or counter in the yellow category.

Orange.$description: A filled pill or counter in the orange category.

Turquoise.$description: A filled pill or counter in the turquoise category.

Red.$description: A filled pill or counter in the red category.

Blue.$description: A filled pill or counter in the blue category. Darkened 7 % from the accent so white ink reaches 4.57:1; no ink reaches 4.5 on the accent itself.

Navy.$description: A filled pill or counter in the navy category.

Green.$description: A filled pill or counter in the green category.

Pink.$description: A filled pill or counter in the pink category.

Yellow.$description: The ink on the yellow fill: the dark ink.

Orange.$description: The ink on the orange fill: the dark ink.

Turquoise.$description: The ink on the turquoise fill: the dark ink.

Red.$description: The ink on the red fill: white.

Blue.$description: The ink on the blue fill: white.

Navy.$description: The ink on the navy fill: white.

Green.$description: The ink on the green fill: the dark ink.

Pink.$description: The ink on the pink fill: white.
